ud6.1:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Vesālī, in the Great Wood, at the Gabled Hall.
ud6.1:1.3: Then the Fortunate One, having dressed in the morning time, after picking up his bowl and robe, entered Vesālī for alms.
ud6.1:1.4: After walking for alms in Vesālī, when he had returned from the alms-round after the meal, he addressed venerable Ānanda, (saying):
ud6.1:1.6: we will go to the Cāpāla shrine to dwell for the day.”
ud6.1:2.1: “Yes, reverend Sir,” said venerable Ānanda, and after replying to the Fortunate One, and taking the sitting mat, he followed along close behind the Fortunate One.
ud6.1:2.2: Then the Fortunate One went to the Cāpāla shrine, and after going, he sat down on the prepared seat.
ud6.1:2.3: While sat the Fortunate One addressed venerable Ānanda, (saying):
ud6.1:3.1: “Delightful, Ānanda, is Vesālī, delightful is the Udena shrine, delightful is the Gotamaka shrine, delightful is the Sattamba shrine, delightful is the Bahuputta shrine, delightful is the Sārandada shrine, delightful is the Cāpāla shrine.
ud6.1:3.2: Whoever has developed, Ānanda, made much of, carried on, established, maintained, augmented, and properly instigated the four paths to power, could, if he wanted, remain for the lifespan or for what is left of the lifespan.
ud6.1:3.3: The Realised One has developed, Ānanda, made much of, carried on, established, maintained, augmented, and properly instigated the four paths to power. If he wanted, Ānanda, the Realised One could remain for the lifespan or for what is left of the lifespan.”
ud6.1:4.1: But venerable Ānanda, despite such a gross hint being made by the Fortunate One, such a gross suggestion being made, was unable to penetrate it,
ud6.1:4.2: and did not beg the Fortunate One, (saying):
ud6.1:4.3: “May the Fortunate One remain, reverend Sir, for the lifespan; may the Happy One remain for the lifespan, for the benefit of many people, for the happiness of many people, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of devas and men,” like one whose mind was possessed by Māra.
ud6.1:4.4: For a second time the Fortunate One addressed venerable Ānanda, (saying):
ud6.1:5.1: “Delightful, Ānanda, is Vesālī, delightful is the Udena shrine, delightful is the Gotamaka shrine, delightful is the Sattamba shrine, delightful is the Bahuputta shrine, delightful is the Sārandada shrine, delightful is the Cāpāla shrine.
ud6.1:5.2: Whoever has developed, Ānanda, made much of, carried on, established, maintained, augmented, and properly instigated the four paths to power, could, if he wanted, remain for the lifespan or for what is left of the lifespan. The Realised One has developed, Ānanda, made much of, carried on, established, maintained, augmented, and properly instigated the four paths to power. If he wanted, Ānanda, the Realised One could remain for the lifespan or for what is left of the lifespan.” But venerable Ānanda, despite such a gross hint being made by the Fortunate One, such a gross suggestion being made, was unable to penetrate it, and did not beg the Fortunate One, (saying): “May the Fortunate One remain, reverend Sir, for the lifespan, may the Happy One remain for the lifespan, for the benefit of many people, for the happiness of many people, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of devas and men,” like one whose mind was possessed by Māra. For a third time the Fortunate One addressed venerable Ānanda, (saying): “Delightful, Ānanda, is Vesālī, delightful is the Udena shrine, delightful is the Gotamaka shrine, delightful is the Sattamba shrine, delightful is the Bahuputta shrine, delightful is the Sārandada shrine, delightful is the Cāpāla shrine. Whoever has developed, Ānanda, made much of, carried on, established, maintained, augmented, and properly instigated the four paths to power, could, if he wanted, remain for the lifespan or for what is left of the lifespan.
ud6.1:5.3: The Realised One has developed, Ānanda, made much of, carried on, established, maintained, augmented, and properly instigated the four paths to power. If he wanted, Ānanda, the Realised One could remain for the lifespan or for what is left of the lifespan.”
ud6.1:6.1: But venerable Ānanda, despite such a gross hint being made by the Fortunate One, such a gross suggestion being made, was unable to penetrate it,
ud6.1:6.2: and did not beg the Fortunate One, (saying):
ud6.1:6.3: “May the Fortunate One remain, reverend Sir, for the lifespan, may the Happy One remain for the lifespan, for the benefit of many people, for the happiness of many people, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of devas and men,” like one whose mind was possessed by Māra.
ud6.1:7.1: Then the Fortunate One addressed venerable Ānanda, (saying):
ud6.1:7.2: “Go, Ānanda, now is the time for whatever you are thinking.”
ud6.1:7.3: “Yes, reverend Sir,” said venerable Ānanda, and after replying to the Fortunate One, rising from his seat, worshipping and circumambulating the Fortunate One, he sat down not far away at the root of a certain tree.
ud6.1:8.1: Then the Wicked Māra, not long after the venerable Ānanda had gone, went to the Fortunate One, and after going, he stood on one side. While stood on one side the Wicked Māra said this to the Fortunate One:
ud6.1:9.1: “May the Fortunate One attain Complete Emancipation, reverend Sir, may the Happy One attain Complete Emancipation, now is the time, reverend Sir, for the Fortunate One’s Complete Emancipation.
ud6.1:9.2: For the Fortunate One, reverend Sir, has said these words:
ud6.1:9.3: ‘I will not attain Complete Emancipation, Wicked One, for as long as my monks are not (true) disciples, accomplished, disciplined, confident, secure, learned, bearers of Dhamma, practicing in conformity with the Dhamma, correct in their practice, living in conformity with the Dhamma, and having learned it from their own teacher, will declare, reveal, make known, set forth, open up, analyse, make plain - after giving a good rebuke with reason to the arguments of others that have arisen - and teach the wonderful Dhamma.’
ud6.1:9.4: But at present, reverend Sir, the Fortunate One’s monks are (true) disciples, accomplished, disciplined, confident, secure, learned, bearers of Dhamma, practicing in conformity with the Dhamma, correct in their practice, living in conformity with the Dhamma, and having learned it from their own teacher, do declare, reveal, make known, set forth, open up, analyse, make plain - after giving a good rebuke with reason to the arguments of others that have arisen - and teach the wonderful Dhamma.
ud6.1:9.5: May the Fortunate One attain Complete Emancipation, reverend Sir, may the Happy One attain Complete Emancipation, now is the time, reverend Sir, for the Fortunate One’s Complete Emancipation.
ud6.1:10.1: For the Fortunate One has said these words:
ud6.1:10.2: ‘I will not attain Complete Emancipation, Wicked One, for as long as my nuns are not (true) disciples, accomplished, disciplined, confident, secure, learned, bearers of Dhamma, practicing in conformity with the Dhamma, correct in their practice, living in conformity with the Dhamma, and having learned it from their own teacher, will declare, reveal, make known, set forth, open up, analyse, make plain - after giving a good rebuke with reason to the arguments of others that have arisen - and teach the wonderful Dhamma.’
ud6.1:10.3: But at present, reverend Sir, the Fortunate One’s nuns are (true) disciples, accomplished, disciplined, confident, secure, learned, bearers of Dhamma, practicing in conformity with the Dhamma, correct in their practice, living in conformity with the Dhamma, and having learned it from their own teacher, do declare, reveal, make known, set forth, open up, analyse, make plain - after giving a good rebuke with reason to the arguments of others that have arisen - and teach the wonderful Dhamma.
ud6.1:10.4: May the Fortunate One attain Complete Emancipation, reverend Sir, may the Happy One attain Complete Emancipation, now is the time, reverend Sir, for the Fortunate One’s Complete Emancipation.
ud6.1:11.1: For the Fortunate One has said these words:
ud6.1:11.2: ‘I will not attain Complete Emancipation, Wicked One, for as long as my male lay followers are not (true) disciples, accomplished, disciplined, confident, secure, learned, bearers of Dhamma, practicing in conformity with the Dhamma, correct in their practice, living in conformity with the Dhamma, and having learned it from their own teacher, will declare, reveal, make known, set forth, open up, analyse, make plain - after giving a good rebuke with reason to the arguments of others that have arisen - and teach the wonderful Dhamma.’
ud6.1:11.3: But at present, reverend Sir, the Fortunate One’s male lay followers are (true) disciples, accomplished, disciplined, confident, secure, learned, bearers of Dhamma, practicing in conformity with the Dhamma, correct in their practice, living in conformity with the Dhamma, and having learned it from their own teacher, do declare, reveal, make known, set forth, open up, analyse, make plain - after giving a good rebuke with reason to the arguments of others that have arisen - and teach the wonderful Dhamma.
ud6.1:11.4: May the Fortunate One attain Complete Emancipation, reverend Sir, may the Happy One attain Complete Emancipation, now is the time, reverend Sir, for the Fortunate One’s Complete Emancipation.
ud6.1:12.1: For the Fortunate One has said these words:
ud6.1:12.2: ‘I will not attain Complete Emancipation, Wicked One, for as long as my female lay followers are not (true) disciples, accomplished, disciplined, confident, secure, learned, bearers of Dhamma, practicing in conformity with the Dhamma, correct in their practice, living in conformity with the Dhamma, and having learned it from their own teacher, will declare, reveal, make known, set forth, open up, analyse, make plain - after giving a good rebuke with reason to the arguments of others that have arisen - and teach the wonderful Dhamma.’
ud6.1:12.3: But at present, reverend Sir, the Fortunate One’s female lay followers are (true) disciples, accomplished, disciplined, confident, secure, learned, bearers of Dhamma, practicing in conformity with the Dhamma, correct in their practice, living in conformity with the Dhamma, and having learned it from their own teacher, do declare, reveal, make known, set forth, open up, analyse, make plain - after giving a good rebuke with reason to the arguments of others that have arisen - and teach the wonderful Dhamma.
ud6.1:12.4: May the Fortunate One attain Complete Emancipation, reverend Sir, may the Happy One attain Complete Emancipation, now is the time, reverend Sir, for the Fortunate One’s Complete Emancipation.
ud6.1:13.1: For the Fortunate One has said these words:
ud6.1:13.2: ‘I will not attain Complete Emancipation, Wicked One, for as long as this spiritual life of mine has not become successful and prosperous, well spread out, possessed by many, become great, until it is well explained amongst devas and men.’
ud6.1:13.3: But at present, reverend Sir, the Fortunate One’s spiritual life is successful and prosperous, well spread out, possessed by many, become great, it is well explained amongst devas and men.
ud6.1:13.4: May the Fortunate One attain Complete Emancipation, reverend Sir, may the Happy One attain Complete Emancipation, now is the time, reverend Sir, for the Fortunate One’s Complete Emancipation.”
ud6.1:14.1: When that was said the Fortunate One said this to the Wicked Māra:
ud6.1:14.2: “You should have little concern, Wicked One, in no long time the Realised One will become completely emancipated,
ud6.1:14.3: after three months have passed from now, the Realised One will attain Complete Emancipation.”
ud6.1:15.1: Then at the Cāpāla shrine the Fortunate One, mindfully, with full awareness, relinquished the life process.
ud6.1:15.2: With the relinquishment of the life process by the Fortunate One there was a great earthquake, and a fearful, horrifying crash of the devas’ (thunder) drum.
ud6.1:16.1: Then the Fortunate One, having understood the significance of it, on that occasion uttered this exalted utterance:
ud6.1:17.2: And the continuation-process the Sage relinquished.
ud6.1:17.4: He broke continuity of self like a coat of mail.”
